output.reason: The changelog line [ev-13b804c336de] says little, but the linked PR [ev-5a7f0f6ed93c] fills in the change. When the hydrator wants an app refreshed, it no longer puts the app straight on the controller's refresh work queue; it sets the refresh annotation instead, "so the correct controller shard picks up the refresh operation." That points the applicability at installations that use the hydrator with a sharded application controller. The consequence class is a fix that needs no operator action: after the upgrade, hydrator-triggered refreshes go to the shard that owns the app. Confidence is low because the PR does not spell out the exposure condition or the exact failure symptom (the linked issue #22055 is not shown), and the changed files [ev-97f519f9a7f2] also touch server/application.go and util/webhook/webhook.go, so the change may reach beyond the hydrator.
